difficultyReason: Short two-sentence stimulus with 'therefore' marking the main conclusion directly. Distractors restate the premise about vaccination rates or overstate the scope.
stimulus: Recent data show that counties offering free booster clinics have vaccination rates nearly twice those of counties without such clinics. Therefore, municipalities that want to raise their local vaccination rates should invest in free booster clinics.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Municipalities that want to raise vaccination rates ought to invest in free booster clinics.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Counties that offer free booster clinics have roughly twice the vaccination rates of counties that do not.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Free booster clinics are the only effective way to raise local vaccination rates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Counties without free booster clinics have unacceptably low vaccination rates.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Investing in free booster clinics always doubles a municipality's vaccination rate.

explanations.correct: The sentence following 'therefore' is the author's recommendation, and (A) paraphrases it without altering scope or modal force.
explanations.B: Restates the premise (the observed correlation), not the conclusion.
explanations.C: Overstates — the argument does not claim that free clinics are the only effective method.
explanations.D: Introduces an evaluative claim ('unacceptably low') the argument never makes.
explanations.E: Overstates the predicted effect; the author recommends investment, not guarantees a doubling.

difficultyReason: Three-sentence argument with 'thus' introducing the main conclusion. Trap answers restate the premise or paraphrase the intermediate factual claim.
stimulus: Lying to a patient about a diagnosis, even to spare feelings, undermines the trust on which the doctor-patient relationship depends. Without that trust, patients will be less willing to disclose symptoms and follow medical advice. Thus, physicians should not lie to their patients, even with good intentions.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patients who are lied to are less likely to follow their physicians' medical advice.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lying to a patient undermines the trust that the doctor-patient relationship depends on.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Physicians ought not to lie to their patients, even when their intentions are good.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A doctor-patient relationship cannot survive any act of deception by the physician.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The good intentions of a physician are irrelevant to evaluating that physician's conduct.

explanations.correct: The sentence after 'thus' is the author's main claim, and (C) paraphrases it faithfully.
explanations.A: Restates a premise about downstream effects of lost trust.
explanations.B: Restates the opening premise about the effect of lying on trust.
explanations.D: Overstates — the argument says lying undermines trust, not that relationships cannot survive any deception.
explanations.E: Generalizes beyond what the argument says about intentions.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence argument ending with 'therefore' plus a hedged recommendation. Traps restate the premise or strip the hedge.
stimulus: Small businesses that adopt cloud-based accounting software report substantially fewer bookkeeping errors than those relying on spreadsheets. Therefore, a small business seeking to reduce its bookkeeping errors should consider switching to cloud-based accounting software.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Spreadsheet-based bookkeeping produces more errors than any other method.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Small businesses using cloud-based accounting software report substantially fewer bookkeeping errors than spreadsheet users.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A small business that wants to reduce bookkeeping errors should consider switching to cloud-based accounting software.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any small business that switches to cloud-based accounting software will eliminate its bookkeeping errors.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cloud-based accounting software is the most affordable option for small businesses.

explanations.correct: (C) paraphrases the post-'therefore' recommendation and preserves the hedged modal ('should consider').
explanations.A: Overstates — the argument compares cloud software to spreadsheets only.
explanations.B: Restates the premise (the observed comparison), not the conclusion.
explanations.D: Overstates — 'should consider switching' is weaker than 'will eliminate errors'.
explanations.E: Introduces affordability, which is never mentioned in the argument.

difficultyReason: Three-sentence argument with 'hence' marking the main conclusion. Trap (B) paraphrases the premise about migration; (E) overstates scope.
stimulus: Several species of songbird that historically wintered in the southern plains have shifted their ranges hundreds of miles north over the past two decades. Wildlife biologists attribute this shift to milder winter temperatures across the plains. Hence, continued warming is likely to produce further northward shifts in these songbirds' winter ranges.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Several songbird species have shifted their wintering grounds hundreds of miles northward over the past two decades.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Biologists believe milder winters are the cause of recent songbird range shifts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ongoing warming is likely to push the wintering ranges of these songbirds still farther north.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Songbird populations in the southern plains will collapse if warming continues.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every bird species that winters in the plains will shift its range northward.

explanations.correct: (C) paraphrases the sentence introduced by 'hence' and preserves its hedged 'likely'.
explanations.A: Restates the opening premise about observed shifts.
explanations.B: Restates the second premise about biologists' explanation.
explanations.D: Introduces a collapse claim the argument never makes.
explanations.E: Overstates — the argument concerns only these songbird species.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence legal-domain argument with 'so' as the conclusion marker. Traps restate the premise and overstate scope.
stimulus: A municipal ordinance that is too vague to give citizens fair notice of what it prohibits cannot be enforced consistently by the courts. So any ordinance whose language fails to give citizens fair notice of the prohibited conduct should be struck down.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ordinances whose language fails to give citizens fair notice of prohibited conduct should be struck down.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vague ordinances cannot be enforced consistently by the courts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Citizens have a legal right to fair notice of the content of every municipal ordinance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Courts that enforce ordinances inconsistently should themselves be reformed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No municipal ordinance is ever sufficiently precise to satisfy constitutional requirements.

explanations.correct: (A) paraphrases the 'so'-clause verbatim in structure, preserving scope and modal force.
explanations.B: Restates the opening premise, not the conclusion.
explanations.C: Introduces a rights claim that is nowhere in the argument.
explanations.D: Shifts the conclusion from the ordinance to the courts themselves.
explanations.E: Overstates — the argument targets only vague ordinances, not all of them.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence economics argument ending with 'therefore' and a policy recommendation. Traps restate the premise and one overstates.
stimulus: When a central bank raises interest rates sharply, consumer borrowing slows and unemployment tends to rise within a year. Therefore, central banks that wish to avoid near-term increases in unemployment should refrain from sharp rate hikes.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Central banks that want to avoid near-term increases in unemployment should refrain from sharp interest rate hikes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sharp increases in interest rates slow consumer borrowing and typically raise unemployment within a year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Central banks should never raise interest rates under any circumstances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Consumer borrowing is the primary driver of unemployment in modern economies.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Avoiding unemployment should be the overriding goal of every central bank.

explanations.correct: (A) paraphrases the recommendation after 'therefore', preserving its conditional scope.
explanations.B: Restates the premise about the effects of rate hikes.
explanations.C: Overstates — the argument targets only sharp rate hikes by banks with a particular goal.
explanations.D: Introduces a claim about primary causation that the argument never makes.
explanations.E: Misstates the argument as prescribing an overarching priority.

difficultyReason: Three-sentence technology argument with 'consequently' marker. Traps include a premise restatement and a wrong-direction paraphrase.
stimulus: A smartphone app that tracks a user's location must request specific permissions from the operating system. Users who review these permissions before installing an app are far less likely to install apps that surreptitiously share location data with third parties. Consequently, users concerned about location privacy should review app permissions before installing any new app.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Users who are concerned about location privacy should review app permissions before installing any new app.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A smartphone app cannot track a user's location without requesting permissions from the operating system.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reviewing app permissions eliminates the possibility that an app will share location data with third parties.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apps that surreptitiously share location data should be removed from app stores.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Operating systems should make app permissions easier for users to interpret.

explanations.correct: (A) paraphrases the recommendation following 'consequently' while preserving its scope.
explanations.B: Restates the opening premise about permissions.
explanations.C: Overstates — 'far less likely' does not equal 'eliminates'.
explanations.D: Introduces a removal recommendation the argument never makes.
explanations.E: Shifts the subject from users to operating systems.

difficultyReason: Three-sentence linguistics argument with 'thus' before the main conclusion. Trap (C) paraphrases a premise; (E) overstates scope.
stimulus: Children raised in households where multiple languages are regularly spoken tend to develop stronger executive-function skills than children raised in monolingual households. Executive function is associated with better academic performance in later grades. Thus, exposure to multiple languages in early childhood appears to confer long-term academic benefits.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Early-childhood exposure to multiple languages appears to yield long-term academic benefits.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Executive function is associated with stronger academic performance in later grades.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children in multilingual households have stronger executive-function skills than children in monolingual households.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All children should be raised in multilingual households.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Monolingual households produce children who perform poorly in school.

explanations.correct: (A) paraphrases the post-'thus' conclusion and preserves the hedged 'appears to'.
explanations.D: Overstates — the argument notes a benefit, not a universal prescription.
explanations.E: Wrong direction — the argument praises multilingual exposure, it does not condemn monolingual households.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence history argument ending with 'therefore'. Traps restate the premise and add a claim the argument does not make.
stimulus: Many innovations credited to a single inventor, such as the telephone and the light bulb, were in fact the result of overlapping work by multiple researchers competing for the same patent. Therefore, histories of technology that focus on lone inventors give a misleading picture of how major innovations actually emerge.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Histories of technology that center on lone inventors present a misleading picture of how major innovations actually arise.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Many innovations attributed to individual inventors were actually the product of multiple researchers competing for the same patent.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The telephone and the light bulb were invented simultaneously by several researchers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Patents should not be awarded to individual inventors when multiple researchers were involved.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Historians of technology are uninterested in collaborative research.

explanations.correct: (A) paraphrases the sentence following 'therefore' while preserving scope.
explanations.B: Restates the premise about overlapping work.
explanations.C: Too specific — the argument uses these as examples, not as the conclusion.
explanations.D: Introduces a patent-policy claim the argument never makes.
explanations.E: Introduces an attitude claim the argument never makes.

difficultyReason: Two-sentence arts argument with 'therefore' and a recommendation. Traps restate the premise and overstate the recommendation.
stimulus: Community theaters that offer a free admission night each month consistently attract larger and more diverse audiences over the course of a season than theaters charging admission for every performance. Therefore, community theaters seeking to broaden their audiences should consider adopting a monthly free admission night.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community theaters aiming to broaden their audiences should consider offering a free admission night once a month.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Community theaters with monthly free admission nights draw larger and more diverse audiences than those charging for every performance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Community theaters ought to make every performance free of charge.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only community theaters with monthly free admission nights will survive financially.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Audience diversity is the most important measure of a community theater's success.

explanations.correct: (A) paraphrases the recommendation after 'therefore' and preserves its hedged 'should consider'.
explanations.B: Restates the premise about observed attendance patterns.
explanations.C: Overstates — the argument recommends one free night, not free admission to all performances.
explanations.D: Introduces a financial-survival claim the argument never makes.
explanations.E: Introduces an evaluative claim the argument never makes.
